SUB-STRAND INDICATORS/EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Demonstrate skills in dealing with environmental challenges
indicator_text: Examine ways of dealing with sanitation challenges in the environment
exemplar: 1. Explain: i. Environment ii. Sanitation 2. Discuss the types of environment (physical and social). 3. Identify some environmental problems, including poor sanitation. 4. Examine cultural practices and their related problems for sanitation in the community. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 5. Discuss the effects of poor sanitation practices 6. Identify different ways of managing sanitation problems. 7. Embark on a project with the aim of managing sanitation problems in the community. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS B7/JHS1 1.1.2.1. Examine the sources of energy. Exemplars: 1. Explain energy. 2. Through the use of internet, videos or pictures, describe the sources of energy in Ghana, including fuel wood, hydro, solar and thermal. 3. In groups, categorise sources of energy into renewable and non-renewable. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 1. Examine the benefits of using renewable energy. 2. Examine the benefits of using non-renewable energy sources. 3. In groups, let learners discuss and design posters to show how different sources of energy are used. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 4. In groups, let learners discuss how sun or wind can be used to heat or perform work. 5. Through group discussion, come out with ways of using energy. 6. In groups, discuss why Ghana sometimes imports energy. STRAND 1: ENVIRONMENT SUB-STRAND 2: MAPPING SKILLS INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Demonstrate a range of mapping skills
indicator_text: Demonstrate skills involved in mapping and locating places in the environment
exemplar: 1. Explain the following concepts: “maps” and “scale”. 2. Identify types of maps, including street maps, maps showing landscape features and national maps using an atlas. 3. Explore the importance of maps to different people, including airline managers, fisherfolk, farmers and, for example, a family which has moved from a rural area to a city. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 4. Identify components of maps, including north arrow, scale, map key allowing representation of physical features (including rivers, lakes, mountains and coastline) and human features (including settlements, plantations and industrial developments) using names, symbols and colours. 5. Sketch a map of the school compound, marking the main features. 6. Locate some important landmarks in the community using maps. For example, the bank is 500 metres north of the Junior High School. STRAND 1: ENVIRONMENT SUB-STRAND 3: UNDERSTANDING OUR NATURAL WORLD INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Show understanding of the world around us
indicator_text: Examine major physical features of the earth
exemplar: 1. Identify some major features of the earth such as mountain ranges, rivers, oceans, hot deserts and tropical rainforest. 2. With the use of maps, find the locations of the following major physical features: i. Mountain ranges, including Akuapim-Togo, Gambaga, Kwahu, Himalayas, Rockies, Andes and Alps ii. Rivers, including the River Bia, Tano, Ankobra, Pra, Densu, Volta, Nile, Niger, Congo, Ganges, Yangtze, Amazon, Mississippi iii. Oceans: Atlantic, Arctic, Southern, Indian, Pacific iv. Hot deserts, including Sahara, Kalahari, Gobi, Arabian v. Tropical rainforests, including the Amazon Rainforest INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 3. Discuss human activities that affect the following features and ways of protecting them: i. Major mountain ranges ii. Rivers iii. Oceans 4. Discuss the effects of plastic pollution on water bodies including streams, ponds, rivers, dams, lakes and oceans. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Assess the issue of natural disasters and their management
indicator_text: Examine natural disasters in the environment.
exemplar: 1. Explain natural disasters. 2. Watch documentaries on some natural disasters. 3. Mention examples of natural disasters, including flood, drought, landslide, wildfire, earthquake and sea erosion. 4. Identify natural disasters in Ghana. 5. Suggest ways to manage disasters. 6. Discuss the role of institutions responsible for early detection and management of natural disasters in Ghana, including Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMA), National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO). STRAND 2: FAMILY LIFE SUB-STRAND 1: ADOLESCENT REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Demonstrate understanding of adolescent behaviour and reproductive health issues
indicator_text: Examine issues on adolescent behaviour and reproductive health
exemplar: 1. Explain the concepts: i. Adolescence ii. Reproductive Health 2. Discuss adolescent behaviours, including chastity that would support reproductive health. 3. Discuss in groups why healthy behaviour during adolescence is important, both for the individual and for the country as a whole. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 4. Invite a resource person, such as a doctor or nurse, to talk about how some adolescent behaviours can harm their reproductive health and cause other problems. 5. Explain changes that adolescents go through (physical, cognitive, social and emotional). 6. Discuss some challenges faced by adolescents. STRAND 2: FAMILY LIFE SUB-STRAND 3: SOCIALISATION INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Exhibit knowledge of the importance of socialisation
indicator_text: Examine the place of socialisation in developing the individual
exemplar: 1. Explain the meaning of socialisation (adapting behaviour to the norms of a culture or society). 2. Explain the terms: i. Agencies ii. Agents 3. Identify the agencies and agents of socialisation, including family, schools, parents and teachers. 4. Discuss the roles of agencies and agents in the socialisation process. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 5. Role-play and embark on a socialising project involving the school and the community. 6. With the use of the Internet, let learners find out the need for socialisation and the challenges associated with it. STRAND 2: FAMILY LIFE SUB-STRAND 4: POPULATION INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Analyse the population structure in Ghana and its related issues
indicator_text: Examine the components of population growth
exemplar: 1. Explain the concept of population growth. 2. Discuss how population in Ghana has changed in the recent past. 3. Compare Ghana’s population growth with that of some other countries in Africa and in the world. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 4. Discuss the following factors of population change: i. Birth rate ii. Death rate iii. Migration 5. Investigate the causes of the following in Ghana: i. High birth rates ii. High death rates STRAND 3: SENSE OF PURPOSE SUB-STRAND 1: SELF-IDENTITY INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Show understanding of self as a unique individual
indicator_text: Exhibit knowledge of self-identity
exemplar: 1. Explain the concepts “self ” and “self-identity” 2. Identify attitudes that enhance self-worth, including self-confidence, can-do spirit and a positive attitude towards life. 3. Identify one’s strengths and weaknesses as unique individual and discuss with one’s peers. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 4. Examine the reasons for knowing oneself including accepting oneself and identification of one’s potential and abilities. 5. Describe how an individual can develop their capabilities, including education and training, counselling, continuous practice, etc. STRAND 4: LAW SUB-STRAND 1: CITIZENSHIP INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Analyse the responsibilities of a citizen
indicator_text: Examine the value of citizenship in nation building
exemplar: 1. Explain the concept of “citizenship”. 2. Discuss the various ways of acquiring citizenship in Ghana, including citizenship by birth, adoption, registration and naturalisation. 3. Examine the responsibilities of a Ghanaian citizen, including obeying rules and regulations, protecting state property, reporting crime, respecting national symbols and payment of taxes, among others. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 4. In groups, discuss good working attitudes, including honesty, willingness to report crime and being punctual and regular at events and at the workplace. 5. Dramatise the various ways (communal labour, reporting crime) citizens contribute to the development of the country. subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Demonstrate knowledge of human resource development in Ghana
indicator_text: Mention ways of developing human resource in Ghana
exemplar: 1. Explain the concepts: i. Human resource ii. Human resource development 2. Discuss the importance of human resource development in Ghana. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 4. Assess the challenges associated with human resource development in Ghana. 5. Suggest solutions to problems facing human resource development in Ghana. STRAND 5: SOCIO-ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT SUB-STRAND 2: FINANCIAL AND INVESTMENT ISSUES INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Demonstrate understanding of social security and pension issues
indicator_text: Examine the importance of social security to the individual
exemplar: 1. Explain the concept of social security. 2. Discuss the features of social security, including the law which established it. 3. Identify types of social security schemes, including the Pension Fund. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 4. Think-pair-share the benefits of social security to the individual 5. Create a poster on the benefits of social security. STRAND 5: SOCIO-ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT SUB-STRAND 3:TOURISM INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Demonstrate knowledge on how tourism and leisure promote national development
indicator_text: Examine the role of tourism and leisure in socio- economic development of Ghana
exemplar: 1. Explain the concepts: i. Tourism ii. Leisure 2. Identify some attractive places or sceneries in your locality. 3. Examine reasons for which people go on tour to different places. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 4. Discuss the economic and social importance of tourism to the nation’s development. 5. Explain challenges faced in the tourism industry. 6. Suggest ways of solving the challenges faced in the tourism industry. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 7. Discuss ways of promoting tourism in Ghana. subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Demonstrate understanding of how Ghana became an independent nation

exemplar: 1. Show documentaries or listen to personal accounts on the 28th February riots in Accra. OR Visit the spot where the ex-servicemen were killed. 2. Examine how the Watson Commission helped the move towards independence. 5. With the use of the Internet or any other sources of information, write down the bio data of the three ex-service men (Sgt. Adjetey, Sgt. Odartey Lamptey and Corporal Attipoe) and how this can inspire learners. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Demonstrate understanding of how Ghana became an independent nation
indicator_text: Recount the formation of the Convention People’s Party (CPP) in 1949
exemplar: 1. With the use of internet/pictures show and discuss pictures of Kwame Nkrumah, Kojo Botsio and K.A. Gbedemah as leaders of the CPP. 2. Discuss the role of other groups, including trade unions, ‘veranda boys’ in the activities of the CPP. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 3. Use resource persons, including retired educationalists, veteran soldiers, retired police officers and senior citizens to tell them about the ‘Positive Action’ OR find out from the community/parents what is meant by ‘Positive Action’. 4. In groups, create a poster on one of the following personalities indicating their bio data including the position they occupied in government: Kwame Nkrumah, K. A. Gbedemah and Kojo Botsio

content_standard_text: Demonstrate understanding of how Ghana became an independent nation
indicator_text: Discuss the recommendations of the Coussey Committee and the outcomes of the 1951, 1954 and 1956 elections
exemplar: 1. Discuss how the Coussey Committee recommendations formed the basis of the 1950 Constitution. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 2. Using sources of evidence including YouTube- https://www.eaumf.org/ ejm-blog/2018/2/15/february-13-1951-gov-sir-charles-arden-clarke- invites-nkrumah-to-form-a-government, discuss the outcome of the 1951 elections and why Kwame Nkrumah was released from prison. 3. Discuss the role of Kwame Nkrumah as leader of government business (1951 up to 1952). INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 4. Examine why a new constitution was drawn up in 1954 (for example, the CPP was dissatisfied with the provisions of the 1950 constitution and called for a new constitution to be drawn up for the Gold Coast). 5. Discuss what happened after the CPP won the 1956 election. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

Explain the factors to be considered in community decision-making process, including investigating, developing and evaluating alternatives. 5. Invite a resource person to talk about the importance of community development. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 6. Identify a specific need or problem of the community and show how learners can help solve it.

subject: Social Studies
indicator_text: Discuss the relevance of volunteerism to community development

Examine the ways by which one can volunteer in the community responsibly, including performing household chores, shopping or cleaning for an elderly person and helping clean the community. 3. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 4. Discuss the importance of volunteerism to socio-economic development of the community. 5. Project work: form voluntary clubs and discuss their functions within the community. 6. Do a voluntary work in the community and write a report on it. Produce a chart showing major political events from 1951 to1960.

Explain how Ghana’s human resource can be efficiently used in the production of goods and services. 5. Investigate how some people in the community use their human resource abilities to help the community develop. 6. Suggest new ways by which they would use their human resource abilities to help develop the community. STRAND 2: FAMILY LIFE SUB-STRAND 2: THE FAMILY INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Evaluate the institution of marriage in Ghana
indicator_text: Examine the importance of marriage as a social institution in Ghana
exemplar: 1. Explain the concept of marriage as a social institution (other social institutions include the family and religious sects). 2. Discuss ways of contracting marriages in Ghana. 3. Identify the ways in which marriage is important as a social institution, including providing a stable, loving setting for children to be brought up and helping to provide economic support for parents. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 4. Investigate the causes of broken marriages. 5. Dramatise the effects of broken marriages on the family structure (such as teenage pregnancy, drug abuse and truancy). 6. Suggest ways of sustaining marriages. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Assess the need for responsible parenting in the family
indicator_text: Examine the importance of responsible parenting within the family system
exemplar: 1. Explain the concepts: i. Parenthood ii. Parenting 2. Differentiate parenthood from parenting. 3. Discuss the responsibilities of parents including providing food, clothes, shelter and a loving and stable environment for the upbringing of children. 4. Discuss inappropriate parenting behaviour and its consequences, including failure to provide the basic needs of children,. For example, drunkenness. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 5. Examine how some behaviours by children can cause their parents to act inappropriately for example, disobedience, indiscipline, refusal to go to school and perform house chores. 6. Suggest ways for handling parent-child conflicts, including dialogue, effective communication 7. Carry out an education programme in the community on the need for parents to be responsible. STRAND 2: FAMILY LIFE SUB-STRAND 4: POPULATION INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Analyse the population structure in Ghana and its related issues
indicator_text: Assess population structure in Ghana and its associated development issues
exemplar: 1. Recap on Basic 8 work on the population structure in Ghana. With the use of the Internet or a chart examine the structure of the Ghanaian population. 2. In groups, analyse the effects of rapid population growth on the family, the community and the nation. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 3. Dramatise the effects of large family size on the up keep of the family 4. Suggest ways in which social problems and rapid population growth could be minimised, including public education on the need for small family sizes. STRAND 3: SENSE OF PURPOSE SUB-STRAND 3: CULTURE AND NATIONAL IDENTITY INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Evaluate the place of culture in national identity
indicator_text: Assess the significance of symbols, music and ceremonies in promoting national identity
exemplar: 1. Explain the concept of national identity. 2. Sing patriotic songs and discuss how songs promote national identity. 3. With the use of videos or pictures, identify some national and traditional symbols and discuss their features and significance. For example, the National Flag, Coat of Arms, the Staff of Office of the President, the Mace, Adinkra and other Ghanaian symbols INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 4. Interpret some national and traditional symbols and evaluate their importance in fostering national unity. 5. Discuss ways of fostering national unity and defending the integrity of the nation. 6. Discuss how national ceremonies can be used to foster national unity. 7. Discuss how respecting the customs and culture of other groups plays a part in celebrating diversity in Ghana and helps draw the whole nation together. For example, festivals such as Homowo celebrated by the Gas, Hogbetsoto by the Anlos, Kundum by the Nzema. STRAND 4: LAW AND ORDER SUB-STRAND 3: THE 1992 CONSTITUTION INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Assess the relevance of the 1992 Constitution
indicator_text: Examine the 1992 Constitution and its significance to national development
exemplar: 1. Explain the meaning of a constitution. 2. Outline the main features of the 1992 Constitution. 3. Use videos or pictures to identify the functions of the three main organs of government (the legislature, the executive and the judiciary). INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS CORE COMPETENCIES 4. subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Assess the relevance of the 1992 Constitution
indicator_text: Discuss the rights of the child as enshrined in the 1992 Constitution
exemplar: 1. Explain the concepts of child rights. 2. Examine the provisions of child rights in the 1992 Constitution. 3. Invite a resource person to discuss the need for children’s rights. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 4. Carry out a project on the responsibilities of children. 5. Explain the concept of child abuse. 6. Identify acts that constitute child abuse, including child labour and early marriages. 7. Examine the effects of child abuse, including physical injury, psychological trauma and poor health. STRAND 4: LAW AND ORDER SUB-STRAND 4: PEACE AND SECURITY IN OUR INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
substrand: PEACE AND SECURITY IN OUR NATION
content_standard_text: Assess the role of peace and security in national development
indicator_text: Examine the relevance of peace and security in our community
exemplar: 1. Explain the concepts of peace and security. 2. Discuss ways of promoting peace and security. 3. With the use of video and pictures, compare a country destroyed by conflict and another that has enjoyed a long period of peace. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 4. Using documentaries and pictures, examine safety measures in the community, including road safety and fire safety. 5. Discuss the importance of peace and security in community development, including the way that it encourages confidence in individuals and investors. 6. Role play how peace can be maintained in your neighbourhood. STRAND 4: LAW AND ORDER 5: PROMOTING DEMOCRACY AND POLITICAL STABILITY INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Show understanding of how to promote democracy and political stability
indicator_text: Examine election as a way of promoting democracy and political stability
exemplar: 1. Explain the concepts of democracy and election. 2. Examine the role of free and fair elections in promoting democracy. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 3. Discuss the processes involved in conducting an election. 4. Identify and discuss the importance of electoral materials. 5. Watch videos of people casting their votes at a polling station peacefully and discuss your observations. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 6. Demonstrate how free and fair elections can be conducted using role-play to elect class leaders. 7. Assess the role of the Electoral Commission. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Demonstrate understanding of the District Assembly concept in Ghana
indicator_text: Examine the role of the District Assembly in promoting decentralisation
exemplar: 1. Explain the concept of decentralisation. 2. Describe the structure of the District Assembly as a decentralised arm of government. 3. Examine the role of District Assemblies in the development of the districts. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 4. Examine the contribution of the Assemblies, including Metropolitan, Municipal, District. 5. Invite a resource person to talk about the workings of the MMDAs.

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Evaluate the importance of political stability in Ghana’s development
indicator_text: Assess the significance of political stability in national development
exemplar: 1. Explain political stability. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 2. Examine the ways of achieving political stability. 3. Through the use of videos and pictures, discuss some of the threats to political stability in the country. For example, vigilantism, political intolerance, abuse of freedom of speech through radio, etc. 4. Discuss the importance of political stability. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 5. Suggest ways of promoting political stability in Ghana. STRAND 5: SOCIO-ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT SUB-STRAND 4: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Analyse the contribution of science and technology to national development
indicator_text: Examine how science and technology can be used to promote development
exemplar: 1. Explain the concepts: i. Science ii. Technology 2. Examine the difference(s) between ‘Science’ and ‘Technology’. 3. Discuss how science and technology can be used for development and production in Ghana. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 4. Examine the role of science and technology in specific sectors of the economy, including mining, education, agriculture and energy generation. 5. With the use of the Internet investigate and make presentations on the role of science and technology in the development of Ghana. 6. Examine the problems impeding the development of science and technology in Ghana. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 7. Suggest ways of promoting science and technology in Ghana. 8. Project: Identify a problem in the school and use the knowledge acquired in science and technology to solve it. STRAND 5: SOCIO-ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT SUB-STRAND 2: FINANCIAL AND INVESTMENT ISSUES INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Show understanding of the provisions under National Pensions Act 766 and PNDC Law 247
indicator_text: Exhibit knowledge on pension rights under National Pensions Act 766 and PNDC Law 247
exemplar: 1. Discuss the provisions under National Pensions Act 766. 2. In small groups, do a presentation on the provisions under PNDC Law 247. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 3. Invite a resource person to talk about social security in Ghana. 4. In small groups, do a presentation on the benefits under the Three Tier Pension Scheme, including Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3. 5. Research the application processes for the various SSNIT benefits. STRAND 6: NATIONHOOD SUB-STRAND 2: THE REPUBLICS INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Demonstrate understanding that Ghana had two republics between 1979 and 2000
indicator_text: Explain how the Third Republic came into being (1979-1981)
exemplar: 1. Use the internet, print media and oral sources to find out how the Third Republic was established. 2. Identify the main political parties that took part in the June 1979 elections and their respective candidates. 3. Discuss the outcome of the June 1979 elections. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 4. With the use of Internet sources, dramatise the handing over of power from the AFRC to Dr Hilla Liman’s People’s National Party. B9/JHS3 6.2.1.2. Explain political developments under the Third Republic Exemplars: 1. Identify the main features of the Third Republican Constitution, including the prohibition of a one-party state, limitation on the influence of the armed forces and the police. 2. Discuss the impact of the Third Republican Constitution on the political development of the country, including the civilisation of the armed forces, promotion of multiparty system and national integration. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 3. Compare the features of the Second and Third Republican Constitution

subject: Social Studies
content_standard_text: Demonstrate understanding that Ghana had two republics between 1979 and 2000
indicator_text: Explain how the Fourth Republic came into being
exemplar: 1. Use the Internet, print media and oral sources to find out how the Fourth Republic was established. 2. Discuss the outcome of the 28 April 1992 referendum. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 3. Identify the political parties that took part in the 1992 elections and their respective leaders. 4. Discuss the nature of the First Parliament of the Fourth Republic, including the boycott of the First Parliament of the Fourth Republic by the largest opposition party (the NPP) at the time. 1. Dramatise the inauguration of the first president of the Fourth Republic. 2. Analyse the 1992 constitution vis-a-vis the American constitution and the Westminster system of government. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS B.9.6.1.1.4. Explain political developments under the Fourth Republic Exemplars: 1. Discuss the features of the Fourth Republican constitution. 2. Debate the pros and cons of the First Parliament of the Fourth Republic. INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS 3. Under the Forth Republic the President is the Head of State, Head of Government and Commander in Chief of the Ghana Armed Forces. Assess the advantages of this arrangement. 4. Compare Ghana’s presidential system of government and the Westminster system in the United Kingdom.
